title: Kinetic-inductance Parametric Amplification in Superconducting Hybrid Magnonics
authors: Pratap Kumar Pal, Moojune Song, Jinho Lim, Juliang Li, Serhii Kruhlov, Ralu Divan, Ulrich Welp, Clarence Chang, Kab-Jin Kim, Valentine Novosad, Axel Hoffmann, Yi Li
abstract: Parametric amplification enables sensitive microwave detection and signal processing by amplifying weak signals with minimal added noise. Here, we demonstrate kinetic inductance mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system comprising a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. The resonator exhibits four wave mixing and nonlinear frequency pulling, enabling parametric amplification both away from and within the magnon-photon strong coupling regime. In the magnon detuned regime, we observe 7 dB gain, while coupling to the YIG magnon shifts the parametric amplification response by ~20 MHz and yields 3.4 dB gain in the hybrid mode. Thus, magnon photon coupling provides a route to magnetically tune the spectral position of kinetic inductance parametric amplification. At higher pump powers, the system transitions to a self oscillatory regime featuring comb-like sidebands and probe activated nonlinear mode mixing. These results establish hybrid magnonics as a platform for tunable nonlinear microwave amplification and dynamics.
summary: This paper demonstrates parametric amplification in a novel superconducting hybrid magnonic system combining a nonlinear nanowire resonator with a YIG sphere. By utilizing four-wave mixing, the authors achieve measurable gain and show that the magnon-photon coupling allows for magnetic tuning of the amplification frequency. This establishes the platform as a versatile tool for nonlinear microwave signal processing.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate and characterize kinetic-inductance-mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system for sensitive, tunable microwave signal processing.
main_result: The system successfully exhibits parametric amplification, achieving up to 7 dB gain in the magnon-detuned regime, and shows that magnon-photon coupling allows for magnetic tuning of the amplification's spectral position.
method: Measurements involve using a superconducting hybrid magnonic resonator coupled to a YIG sphere, employing four-wave mixing (4WM) pumping and scanning spectroscopy (SA) techniques.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a hybrid magnonic system consisting of a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a YIG sphere. The nonlinearity arises from the kinetic inductance of the superconducting nanowire.
key_observables: Gain (in dB), frequency shift ($\sim 20 	ext{ MHz}$), and the observation of comb-like sidebands in the self-oscillatory regime.
important_parameters: Pump power ($P_{	ext{pump}}$), external biasing magnetic field ($H$), and the coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the 4WM mechanism and the ability to tune the system near the magnon-photon degeneracy point; quantitative analysis of self-oscillation requires assumptions about intrinsic nonlinearity and damping rate.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device setup, VNA spectra showing magnon-photon mode anti-crossing, SA heatmaps demonstrating 4WM and frequency pulling, and spectra confirming the transition to self-oscillation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first demonstrating the basic 4WM mechanism, then characterizing the gain in the magnon-detuned regime, followed by analyzing the effect of magnon-photon coupling, and finally exploring the rich dynamics in the self-oscillatory regime at high pump powers.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization of tunable nonlinear microwave amplification using magnonics, which is highly relevant for developing quantum sensors and quantum microwave circuits by coupling superconducting electronics to magnetic excitations.

Spintronics.note: The paper directly concerns a hybrid magnonic system (YIG sphere coupled to a superconducting resonator) exhibiting parametric amplification, which falls squarely into the realm of magnon-photon coupling and nonlinear microwave signal processing central to spintronics.
